Pong, Breakout, and falling-object catching games fit poorly because the agent-position structure is not confined to a paddle track. A static maze-navigation game does not explain the moving-object weights as well. Sokoban is a possible alternative, but distributed collectibles and temporal information favor a moving-adversary collection game.

The weights do not uniquely establish the game’s rules, and the sparse output pathways limit how confidently one can reconstruct behavior.
